title: Reduced Fat Milk, 2% Milkfat, with Added Vitamin A and Vitamin D

content.title: About
content.content: Reduced fat milk with 2 % milkfat is a liquid dairy product obtained from cow's milk after partial removal of fat. It is fortified with vitamins A and D, enhancing its nutritional value.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Milk with 2 % milkfat is often called “semi‑skim” and is seen as a compromise between whole and skim milk.
Vitamin A in milk supports vision and the immune system.
Vitamin D aids calcium absorption and bone health.
Reduced‑fat milk retains most of the protein, calcium, and other minerals found in whole milk.
In Russia and many CIS countries, such products are commonly labeled as “milk 2 %”.

items.title: Rich in calcium
items.content: Milk is one of the best dietary sources of calcium, essential for strong bones and teeth.

items.title: High‑quality protein source
items.content: Milk protein contains all essential amino acids, supporting tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Immune support
items.content: Vitamin A boosts immune response, while vitamin D regulates immune cell activity.

items.title: Helps prevent osteoporosis
items.content: The combination of calcium and vitamin D promotes bone density maintenance.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: At 2 % milkfat, the product is less caloric than whole milk while retaining most nutrients.

items.title: Lactose intolerance
items.content: People lacking sufficient lactase may experience bloating, gas, and diarrhea after consuming milk.

items.title: Cow‑milk allergy
items.content: Allergic reactions can range from skin rashes to anaphylaxis and require complete avoidance.

items.title: Hormone and antibiotic residues
items.content: In some regions milk may contain trace hormones or antibiotics; choosing certified organic products can mitigate this risk.

items.title: Excess vitamin A intake
items.content: Too much vitamin A can be toxic, especially for children and pregnant women.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: 2 % milk can be drunk plain, added to cereals, smoothies, baked goods, sauces, and coffee. Fortification with vitamins A and D makes it a beneficial addition to children's diets and to those needing bone support.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store milk in the refrigerator at 1–4 °C. Once opened, consume within 5–7 days and do not leave at room temperature for more than 2 hours.
